1. Set a daily allowance, a default session length, and a real-life goal.
2. Choose at least one protected app or website.
3. Make Voward the device owner from a computer, once. Allow alarms & reminders so a session ends at the second it was quoted for. Uninstall protection and notifications are optional.
4. Create a recovery key, then choose the deactivation cooldown and how long you will have to confirm deactivation afterward.
5. Review the setup summary and activate protection.

At the gate, name a specific purpose and choose 1–60 minutes. Start the circular pause, then review the plan and explicitly choose Open intentionally or Not now. Finishing the timer never opens protected content automatically. You can configure three alternatives in Settings; choosing one leaves the protected content, returns you Home, and is counted in Progress.

One allowance second buys one second of approved protected use. A session ends at the smaller of its planned duration or the allowance remaining when it starts. Unused allowance carries forward only up to one daily allowance, and the balance never becomes negative. Repeat entries increase only the next pause; they do not change the cost of a quoted session. A session also ends if the phone restarts. With notifications allowed, End session now on the session notification stops it early.

The Progress tab shows measured protected-use time, sessions, early exits, limits reached, the most common session start time, and the most frequently chosen alternative for the current week. Completed daily summaries are kept locally for up to 14 days. Voward does not estimate time saved or infer wellbeing, urges, or health outcomes.

Choose apps from the installed-app picker. For websites, example.com covers that domain and subdomains; example.com/news covers that path and its subtree; and a configured query must match exactly. A strict rule stays blocked regardless of remaining allowance. While protection is active, rules can only become more restrictive: you may add new rules or mark existing rules strict, but you cannot remove rules or turn strict mode off.

Grayscale is automatic for approved sessions in regular restricted apps and websites after a one-time ADB permission grant; there is no separate in-app switch. Strict rules never open, so grayscale does not apply to them. To enable it:
1. Install Android Platform Tools on a computer.
2. On the phone, enable Developer options and USB debugging, connect it to the computer, and approve the debugging prompt.
3. Run: adb shell pm grant com.example.voward android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
4. Open Voward → Settings → Advanced and data and confirm that it says “Grayscale reminder available.”
Voward restores the previous Android color-correction setting when the approved session ends. To revoke access, run: adb shell pm revoke com.example.voward android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

Voward reads which apps are installed and, with usage access, how long one was in the foreground during an approved session. It never reads your screen. Website rules are sent to your browser as enterprise policy and enforced there. Rules, settings, and usage counters stay on-device. Configuration export includes the configured cooldown and confirmation-period durations, but excludes the recovery key, active-protection state, pending deactivation request and timestamps, current allowance balance, usage counters, and temporary approvals. Import is unavailable while protection is active and cannot restore a pending request. Purpose text entered at the gate is not stored.

The default deactivation policy is a 24-hour cooldown followed by a 1-hour confirmation period. Cooldown choices are 0, 1 minute, 6 hours, 12 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, or 72 hours; confirmation-period choices are 1, 2, 3, 6, 12, or 24 hours. These settings can be changed only while protection is inactive. With a positive cooldown, enter the recovery key once to request deactivation. Protection and uninstall friction remain active while waiting. You can cancel the request immediately without the key. The confirmation period begins and expires silently: there is no notification, sound, vibration, badge, background polling, or automatic deactivation. During this period, enter the key again, press Deactivate protection, and accept the final confirmation. Incorrect keys do not change the deadline. If the confirmation period expires, the complete process must be restarted. Eligibility uses monotonic device time; a detected clock shift over two minutes or a reboot invalidates the request. With cooldown 0, one correct key, an explicit button press, and final confirmation deactivate without creating a request. Critical emergency and device-recovery apps cannot be selected for protection. If Voward stops running altogether, the dead man switch releases every restriction on its own after the number of days you set.
Strict rules ignore the remaining allowance. Access stays blocked until you deactivate protection.

Removes the reset option from Settings. The recovery-mode reset still works, so you are never locked out, but OEM unlocking is disabled until you deactivate.

A cable and a computer are how you recover this phone if Voward stops working. With this on, that route is closed until you deactivate with your recovery key.

Device owner: not set up. Nothing on this screen is enforced until it is.
The real-life reason you are doing this. Shown on the Today screen and at the gate, so you see it at the moment you are deciding. It is never sent anywhere.
Three things you can do instead. They appear as buttons at the gate; choosing one returns you to the home screen. Leave them blank to hide the buttons.

Locked while protection is active. Total minutes of approved use per day, across all regular rules. One allowance second buys one second of use. Unused time carries over up to one full day worth. Strict rules ignore it entirely.

Locked while protection is active. The session length pre-selected at the gate. You can still choose 1 to 60 minutes each time. A session ends at whichever is smaller: your chosen length, or the allowance you have left.

Locked while protection is active. How long you wait at the gate before the Open button appears, on your first entry of the day. The app never opens anything automatically when the timer reaches zero — you still have to choose.
Locked while protection is active. How much the pause grows each time you come back the same day, as a percentage. At zero the pause never grows. The pause is capped at one hour regardless.

The only in-app way to turn protection off. Stored as a salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash — it cannot be displayed or recovered, by you or by anyone else. Write it down somewhere outside this phone before you activate. Losing it means waiting out the dead man switch or wiping the device.

Locked while protection is active. How long you must wait after requesting deactivation before you can confirm it. Protection stays fully active throughout, and you can cancel at any point without the key. Set it to 0 to deactivate immediately after confirming.

Locked while protection is active. How long you have to finish deactivating once the cooldown ends. The window opens and closes silently — no notification, no reminder. Miss it and the request is deleted and you start over. A shorter window is stronger protection.

Your safety net. If the app fails a health check for this many days in a row, every restriction releases itself automatically, without the recovery key. This is what saves you from a crash loop or a bad update. Shortening it weakens protection; lengthening it increases the risk of being stuck. Default 14 days.

Shows whether Voward is the device owner. Without it, nothing on this screen can be enforced — apps can be uninstalled and website rules do nothing. Setting it up needs a computer, once; see the installation guide.

Stops Voward being uninstalled, force-stopped, or having its data cleared from Settings. Enforced by Android, not by Voward, so it holds even when the app is not running. Released by the normal key-and-cooldown flow.
Safe mode starts Android with third-party apps disabled, which would otherwise switch protection off with a single reboot. This closes that. Normal reboots are unaffected.

A second user, a guest session, a work profile, or a private space each get their own copy of your apps, outside these rules. This blocks creating them. Existing profiles must be removed before you can provision the device at all.
Rolling the clock forward would refill your daily allowance. This forces automatic network time and blocks manual changes. Time-zone changes are unaffected, so travelling is fine.

Removes the reset option from Settings. It does not block the recovery-mode reset — the hardware key combination always works, so you are never locked out of your own phone. It also disables the OEM-unlocking toggle, so you cannot unlock the bootloader until you deactivate.

Removes one of your escape routes. ADB is how you would recover this phone from a computer if something went wrong. Turning it off closes the last manual bypass; leaving it on means anyone with a cable and your unlocked phone has more options. Off by default.

Website rules are enforced inside the browser itself, through Android managed configuration, so they work in fullscreen, across redirects, and in links opened from other apps. A browser Voward cannot configure is paused rather than filtered: the icon stays, but opening it shows a message. Some browsers honour the rules without advertising it, so you can test any of them and decide for yourself. You do not have to uninstall anything.

A regular rule asks for a purpose and a pause before opening. A strict rule cannot be opened at all while protection is active — no gate, no allowance, no exception. While protection is active you can add rules and make them strict, but you cannot remove them or make them regular again.

Addresses and paths, matched by the browser rather than by reading the screen. A rule for a domain covers its subdomains. Keyword rules match page text and have no equivalent inside a browser, so a new one is refused and any you wrote earlier is no longer enforced — the rules screen names them.

Optional allowance reminders. During an approved session the notification counts down and carries End session now, which is the only way to stop a session before its deadline. Deactivation is deliberately silent — you will never be notified that your confirmation window has opened.

Ends an approved session at the second it was quoted for. Android does not grant this automatically, and without it the deadline is an inexact alarm that the system may hold back — a five minute session measured six minutes on a Pixel 10. The session still ends, just late.

Lets Voward measure how long you actually spent in an app, so a session ends on time. Granted from Android Settings, not from a computer. Without it, sessions end on the clock rather than on real use, and you are charged the full length you asked for.
Turns the screen grayscale during an approved session and restores your previous setting afterwards. Needs a one-time permission granted from a computer; everything else works without it.
Applies every rule and restriction above. Requires at least one rule, a positive allowance, and a recovery key. From this point, timing settings are locked and rules can only be tightened.
Clears today counters. It does not restore spent allowance. Unavailable while protection is active.

Gives up device ownership so Voward can be uninstalled normally. Android will not let you uninstall a device owner app at all, so without this the only way off would be a factory reset. Available only once protection is off.
Strict rules cannot be opened while protection is active.

Any newly installed app is paused once and you decide whether to keep it. This catches clones and web wrappers that would otherwise slip past your rules. You can still install anything you want.

Any newly installed app is paused once, and you decide whether to keep it or make it a rule. This catches web wrappers and clones that would otherwise slip past your rules — without it, installing the same thing under a different name is the cheapest way around every rule you have. You can still install anything you want, from Play or elsewhere. Only applies while protection is active.
